thread:
maria: quick question: for penalty calculations do we keep admission snapshots in the sidecar or mirror to a ledger?
kevin: sidecar = lowest p99. ledger = easier global reasoning. tradeoff is sync vs correctness.
jen: hybrid seems right: sidecar decides fast, streams diffs to ledger async. ledger for audits & reconciliation.
lucy: agree. make admit responses include a compact admit_token so we can reconcile later.
maria: admit_token idea: {epoch, shard, seq}. small and map to quota shard to avoid extra topology.
kevin: batch ledger writes per-epoch (1s) to cut QPS. ledger stores per-tenant epoch aggregates not every request.
jen: reconciliation worker reads admit_tokens and compares to ledger epoch totals. if over-admit detected, escalate: soft throttle -> stricter throttles.
lucy: need safety: require multiple reconciliation hits before hard blocks to avoid flapping. propose 3 hits in 30s window.
admit-bot: CI job scheduled: admit-token-ledger-unit-tests (CI#6789)
maria: rollout plan: sidecar-only -> enable admit_token -> enable ledger mirror canary -> reconciliation worker -> tune thresholds.
kevin: ops items: metric reconcile_lag, reconcile_adjust_rate, and a sidecar mirror kill-switch to fall back to sidecar-only on errors.
jen: security: redact tenant ids in ledger unless KMS is enabled. compliance will ask for retention TTL.
maria: i'll draft a short RFC addendum with data model + migration steps. owners: maria (RFC), jen (recon worker), kevin (telemetry), lucy (shard mapping). aim for canary next week. :thumbsup:
